title: Reachability and optimal-time certificates for quantum control
abstract: Finite-time control is central to quantum technologies, yet rigorous limits on reachable targets and optimal control times remain largely unknown. We develop a framework for finite-time reachability and optimal-time certificates in constrained quantum control based on moment relaxations with implicitly time-dependent differential constraints. For fixed control horizons and control constraints, the method yields rigorous upper bounds on achievable terminal fidelities, lower bounds on the optimal control times required to reach them, and certificate gaps for benchmarking explicit control pulses. We demonstrate the versatility of our framework in three use cases: entangled-state preparation in two and three qubits, one-qubit gate synthesis across different control geometries, and excitation transfer in an $N$-qubit $XX$ chain. Our work establishes differential moment hierarchies as a practical tool for certifying reachability limits and optimal control times in quantum control, providing hardware-aware quantum speed limits while highlighting structure exploitation as a key ingredient for scalable certification.
summary: The paper introduces a novel framework using differential moment relaxations to rigorously certify the limitations of finite-time quantum control. It calculates upper bounds on achievable fidelities and lower bounds on minimum required times for tasks like state preparation and gate synthesis. This provides 'hardware-aware' speed limits, distinguishing true physical constraints from mere optimization shortcomings.
main_problem: The core problem is developing rigorous mathematical certificates for determining the maximum achievable fidelity (reachability) and the minimum time required to reach a target state or gate in constrained quantum control.
main_result: The authors establish differential moment hierarchies that provide computable upper bounds on terminal fidelities and corresponding lower bounds on optimal control times, thereby certifying dynamical limitations.
method: The framework employs moment relaxations applied to noncommutative polynomial optimization problems with implicitly time-dependent differential constraints, formulated as Semidefinite Programs (SDPs).
model_or_system: The work analyzes controlled quantum dynamics governed by Hamiltonians $H(t) = H_0 + \sum u_j(t)H_j$, applied to tasks like state preparation (Bell/GHZ states), gate synthesis ($	ext{SU}(2)$ evolution), and excitation transfer in spin chains.
key_observables: Terminal fidelities ($F_{\Phi^+}, F_{	ext{gate}}, F_{	ext{tr}}$) are the primary observables, alongside the optimal control time $T^\star$.
important_parameters: Control constraints ($\sum u_j^2 \le U_{\max}^2$), relaxation order ($d$), and target fidelity threshold ($\eta$).
main_assumptions: The method relies on moment relaxation techniques, which provide upper bounds; the quality of these bounds depends on the chosen relaxation order $d$.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the geometry of reachable sets, showing how nested convex outer approximations (from the hierarchy) bound the true set, and compare certified lower/upper bounds for state preparation fidelity vs. time.
paper_structure: The paper develops a unified framework by first establishing the mathematical machinery (moment relaxations with differential constraints), then applying it to specific physical tasks: state preparation, gate synthesis, and state transfer, demonstrating how structural symmetries reduce computational complexity.
why_interesting: This work provides powerful, mathematically rigorous tools for quantum control that move beyond purely numerical optimization by providing certified limits on performance, which is crucial for designing fault-tolerant quantum hardware protocols.
